name: Groq
summary: Inference-chip company pursuing lower-latency, lower-cost AI serving.
overview: Groq designs hardware and cloud services optimized for AI inference.
bull_case: Inference demand may become enormous, rewarding specialized speed and efficiency.
bear_case: Nvidia, hyperscalers, and rapid model changes create an unforgiving hardware market.

intelligence.description: Groq operates an AI inference cloud built around its low-latency Language Processing Unit technology.
company: Groq originally developed specialized hardware for fast, low-cost AI inference and later expanded into a global cloud service.
In December 2025 it entered a non-exclusive technology licensing agreement with NVIDIA while continuing to operate independently under new leadership.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Groq is a rare case study in how a private AI infrastructure company can monetize technology without a full acquisition. The structure matters for founders and investors across inference, chips and cloud infrastructure.

changed.text: Licensed inference technology to NVIDIA on a non-exclusive basis; the company remained independent.
Raised $650M to expand its inference cloud footprint and capacity.

takeaways: The NVIDIA agreement validates inference as a strategic bottleneck.
GroqCloud remains a separate operating business after the licensing deal.
The current valuation was not disclosed with the 2026 financing.
